body: Large language models are increasingly used to annotate datasets for training smaller, task-specialized models such as named entity recognition. While this method yields effective models, it assumes that the synthetic dataset is correctly annotated. In this work, we find that (i) current fine-tuning processes simply ignore LLM-introduced annotation noise, resulting in degraded performance and (ii) existing noise-robust losses are not transferable to sequence labeling because annotation noise in named entity recognition is heterogeneous: for example, missing mentions and type errors affect the training signal in different ways. Treating all noisy tokens equally in noise-robust losses and applying a single reweighing criterion for all may therefore remove useful supervision or reinforce incorrect labels. To address this limitation, we propose error-type-aware loss reweighting for NER, which introduces separate reweighing rules for different types of potentially erroneous tokens. Our approach is simple and efficient, does not require additional training resources, and improves F1 by 0.8 - 2.0 percentage points on dataset-level average for noise levels between 15% and 40%, with a maximum improvement of 4.6 percentage points with 24.1% noise on Wikigold.
summaryZh: 本文针对利用LLM标注数据进行NER任务微调时产生的噪声问题，提出了一种错误类型感知的损失重加权方法。研究发现，现有的噪声鲁棒损失函数在处理NER任务时效果不佳，因为不同类型的标注错误（如漏标、类型错误）对模型的影响不同。该方法通过为不同错误类型设置独立的重加权规则，有效提升了模型在噪声数据下的表现，在Wikigold数据集上实现了显著的F1分数提升。
